solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's bound to be instructive to pupils

definitions.text: It's bound to be instructive to pupils

parts.words: It's bound to be instructive to pupils
parts.note: reads like a claim that something will surely educate, but 'bound' is literal: a bound volume written for teaching children

explanation.surface: A confident prediction that something will certainly educate the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' looks like 'certain to be'; it actually describes the binding of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A text used in class is a bound volume whose purpose is teaching pupils.

clue.text: Gleam noticed around top of hill

indicators.note: around says the word for noticed goes round the other letter

parts.note: noticed means seen

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter in a down clue

explanation.surface: A shine spotted on the summit of a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts SEEN round H, the 'top of hill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a soft shine or lustre on a surface; synonym.

clue.text: Principals cheered as hat tossed around

indicators.note: letters tossed around are thrown about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: School heads applauded as a hat is thrown in the air, perhaps at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed around' rearranges the twelve letters of CHEERED AS HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal is the person in charge of a school or college; synonym.

clue.text: Some solids, foul-smelling

indicators.note: some of the word means only part of its letters are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A remark that certain solid substances stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from inside 'solids'. The answer is an uncommon word, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Olid is a rare dictionary adjective for having a rank, offensive odour.

clue.text: Highland mountain lass spotted cat

parts.note: Ben is the Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
gal is an informal word for a girl or lass

explanation.surface: A girl on a Scottish peak catches sight of a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' looks like 'saw'; it describes the cat's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bengal is a domestic cat breed with a leopard-like spotted coat; example.

clue.text: Delivery? Not on holiday

parts.note: off is the opposite of on
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Someone says a parcel will not arrive because they are away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an off break is a ball bowled to turn from the off side, so 'Delivery' is a bowled ball, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket every ball bowled is a delivery, and this spin ball is one kind; example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Scientist, all agitated, sparkles

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up and settle in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An excited scientist is buzzing with brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges SCIENTIST plus ALL; 'all' is part of the fodder as well as the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle is to give off flashes of light, or to be lively and witty; synonym.

clue.text: Elephant fleeing circus finally in the Spanish fairy story

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word in

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a fairy story is a made-up tale, a lie

explanation.surface: An elephant escapes from the circus into a Spanish fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nellie the Elephant' is a British children's song in which the elephant packs her trunk and leaves the circus. 'circus finally' looks like S; it is 'finally in' that gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine is the elephant who says goodbye to the circus; a reference to a well-known character.

clue.text: Delight in account, missing the start

indicators.note: missing the start says the first letter of the word for account is dropped

parts.note: a relation is an account or narration of events

explanation.surface: Pleasure found in a story that lacks its opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'account' is a story, not a bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great joy or high spirits; synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Female is cutting, firstly, man's sheet of film

indicators.note: firstly takes the opening letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: he is a man's pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman is slicing up a man's piece of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firstly' applies to both 'is' and 'cutting', giving I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiche is a flat sheet of microfilm holding pages of reduced text; synonym.

clue.text: Intestate after deductions in odd places and after tax etc

indicators.note: deducting the letters in odd places leaves only the even-numbered letters of the word

explanation.surface: Talk of a dead person's estate, without a will, after taxes and deductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after deductions in odd places' removes the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of INTESTATE. 'Intestate' suggests probate; it is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nett, the British spelling of net, describes an amount remaining once tax and charges are taken off.

clue.text: Part loan arranged for the proprietor?

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A partial loan set up on behalf of the owner of a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges PART LOAN. A patron can be the owner of a hotel or restaurant in British usage, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to a patron, and Collins lists patron as a British word for the owner of a hotel or restaurant.

clue.text: Multi-player sport: note, yours truly's keen!

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
yours truly means I, and I's read as 'I is' becomes 'I am', giving am
game means willing or keen, as in 'I'm game'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that they are eager to play a sport involving many players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly' is the setter, so 'yours truly's' is 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport played by sides of several players, such as football, is played by a team; description.

clue.text: Good fellow, bitter perhaps, and tired

parts.note: a saint is a good person, abbreviated St
bitter is a kind of ale, an English beer

explanation.surface: A decent chap with a pint of beer, and worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' is a British pale beer, not a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale means lacking freshness or worn out from overwork, as in jaded; synonym.

clue.text: Sibling also pruned fibre-producing plants

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a sibling

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the word also loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A sister also cut back some plants grown for fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pruned' is a gardening word for trimming, and here it cuts the end off 'also'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is an agave grown for the strong fibre in its leaves, used for rope and matting; example.

clue.text: "A" team in reserve

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: The first team is being held back as reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'A team' look like the top team; the A is simply the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Money set aside or put aside is kept in reserve for later; synonym phrase.

clue.text: Quietly, RE class is primed in advance

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
RE is religious education, a school subject
a set is a class of pupils grouped by ability

explanation.surface: A religious education class is quietly made ready ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the British school name for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: Something preset has been configured or readied beforehand; synonym.

clue.text: Singular thank you for overcoming head of Machiavellian plotters

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: overcoming is read as coming over, so the word for thank you goes round the other letter

parts.note: cheers is a British informal thank you

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A single thanks for getting the better of a Machiavellian leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Machiavellian plotters' looks like the definition, but 'head of' takes its first letter; the definition is 'plotters'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter is a person who devises secret schemes or intrigues; synonym.

clue.text: Cold, boy gets dressed

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A chilly lad puts some clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, meaning wearing clothes; synonym.

clue.text: First of documents to bring up is dull

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word documents

parts.note: to rear is to bring up a child

explanation.surface: The first paperwork that must be raised is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring up' suggests raising a topic; it means raising children.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning gloomy and dull; synonym.

clue.text: Vessel's blue deck recalled regularly

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the words blue deck run backwards
regularly takes every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A ship's blue deck is mentioned again at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of BLUE DECK, LEEK, and 'recalled' (called back) turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A keel is a flat-bottomed boat or barge, especially a coal barge on the Tyne; a lesser-known sense.

clue.text: Spanish poet's part in madrigal — or cantata

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the poet to the wordplay

indicators.note: part in means a run of letters is taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A Spanish poet has a role in some piece of choral music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in' takes letters across 'madrigal' and 'or', ignoring the dash. Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca (1898-1936) was a celebrated Spanish poet and dramatist; example.

clue.text: Extraordinary respect for monarch's staff

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the usual order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Remarkable deference shown to the people working for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees; it is a rod. SPECTRE is a tempting wrong anagram that the definition rules out.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod carried by a sovereign as an emblem of authority; description.

clue.text: Aid to growth of fir trees replanted around one lake

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the other two
replanted means the trees are put back in a new arrangement, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Something that helps conifers grow after being moved round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replanted' rearranges FIR TREES, and 'around' puts that round I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Manure or chemical feed added to soil helps plants grow; description.
